transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

A hob that intermittently trips the electrics is not normal and should be checked. With an induction hob, likely causes include an internal fault, damaged/loose wiring at the hob or cooker connection, moisture, or an earth-leakage fault causing the RCD to trip.

What to do:

• Notice what has actually tripped at the consumer unit/fuse box:
• a breaker labelled cooker/hob suggests a circuit overload/short fault;
• an RCD/RCBO or the main switch/RCD affecting several circuits suggests earth leakage, often from an appliance.
• When it trips, turn the hob off at its isolator switch (usually a wall switch near the cooker), then reset the breaker/RCD.
  Don’t keep resetting it repeatedly if it trips again.
• Avoid using the hob unattended, and stop using it entirely if there is burning smell, buzzing/crackling, heat at the wall switch, scorch marks, or it trips immediately on switching on.
• Arrange a qualified electrician to test the hob circuit, isolator, and supply cable, and potentially a Hisense appliance engineer to test the hob itself. An electrician can establish whether the fault is in the fixed wiring or the appliance.

It can help to note whether it happens:
• when switching the hob on versus after cooking for a while;
• on a particular ring or power level;
• with certain pans;
• when another high-load appliance is running.

Because it happens only weekly, it may be an intermittent insulation/earth-leakage issue, which generally won’t be solved safely by changing a fuse or simply resetting the consumer unit.
Thanks. There was a faint electrical smell once after it tripped, but nothing since. Does that change what I should do?

Yes — a faint electrical or “burning plastic” smell after a trip makes this more urgent.

Stop using the hob for now and switch it off at the cooker/hob isolator switch, if you have one. Do not just rely on the controls being off. If the isolator, hob cable, plug/socket (if applicable), or consumer unit feels warm, looks discoloured, crackles, or smells burnt, leave it switched off and arrange an electrician urgently. If there is smoke, sparking, or signs of fire, turn off power only if safe to do so and call emergency services.

The smell could come from a loose/high-resistance connection heating up, damaged wiring, an internal hob component, or the cooker switch/terminal. These faults can be intermittent but can worsen and present a fire risk.

Arrange a qualified electrician to inspect the hob circuit, isolator switch, connections, and consumer unit, and have the hob manufacturer/service engineer involved if the fixed wiring tests OK. Tell them it is an induction hob that intermittently trips the RCD/breaker and that there was an electrical smell after one trip.

Until it has been checked, use an alternative cooking method if possible.
